# Objective 2 — final output (Tamil Nadu)

*Plant: 100 L tank, 2.0 m² collector, 175 L/day of 45 °C water. Generated by `scripts/c25_final_output_table.py` from the sealed Objective-2 contract (`results/common100L_<hash>/o3_environment_contract_tamilnadu.json`); every number is read from it.*

## 1. Final design per regime (the main output)

| Regime | Recommendation | PCM | Capsule size | Capsules | PCM share of tank | Layout | PCM mass |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | **PCM tank** | PureTemp 58 | 40 mm radius | 140 | 39.8 % | staggered | 33.4 kg |
| 1 | **PCM tank** | RT57HC | 40 mm radius | 140 | 39.8 % | staggered | 33.8 kg |
| 2 | **PCM tank** | RT57HC | 40 mm radius | 140 | 39.8 % | staggered | 33.8 kg |

All designs use a flow of 0.030 kg/s. The hottest temperatures stay inside the safety limits: PCM about 62 °C (limit 65 °C) and water about 72 °C (limit 75 °C).

Tamil Nadu has three climate regimes, and the PCM tank was recommended in all three; no regime fell back to a water-only tank. The capsule size is the inner radius (outer diameter 81.6 mm). Both the 40 mm radius and the 40 % PCM-share cap are at their upper limits, so this is the corner of the search box.

## 2. What the PCM tank delivers (one-shot test on 2006–2010, run once)

| Regime | PCM | Extra heat over a plain tank | Years PCM wins | Extra overheat-guard hours |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | PureTemp 58 | 137 kWh/yr | 5 of 5 | +937 h/yr |
| 1 | RT57HC | 122 kWh/yr | 5 of 5 | +627 h/yr |
| 2 | RT57HC | 134 kWh/yr | 5 of 5 | +998 h/yr |

The PCM tank beats the plain tank on delivered energy in every test year of every regime, but spends more hours in the overheat guard, because the capsules take the place of water in the fixed 100 L tank.

## 3. Where the MATLAB and ANSYS outputs are

**MATLAB (checkpoint M1), one folder per regime.** Each has the seven what-if designs (the optimum, max of everything, min of everything, a real funnel finalist, only 30 capsules, 10 % and 50 % of the optimum) shown as: a discharge test, three real weather days (clear, average, cloudy), an annual ranking, the four Objective-1 PCMs, and three animated tank cut-aways. It visualises the simulator's own output; it is not a separate MATLAB model.

| Regime | PCM | Folder | Contents |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | PureTemp 58 | `results/m1/figures/` | 6 figures + 3 animations |
| 1 | RT57HC | `results/m1_regime1/figures/` | 6 figures + 3 animations |
| 2 | RT57HC | `results/m1_regime2/figures/` | 6 figures + 3 animations |

Data behind the figures: the CSV files and `manifest.json` in the parent folder (`results/m1/`, `results/m1_regime1/`, `results/m1_regime2/`). Rebuild: `python scripts/c20_m1_export.py --regime k`, then `M1_DIR=results/<folder> matlab -batch "run('matlab_m1/m1_main.m')"`.

**ANSYS Fluent seven-criteria study: regime 0 only** (`ansys/criteria_0_optimal_reference/` … `ansys/criteria_6_50pct_of_optimal/`, summary in `ansys/criteria_common/`). Whole-tank and single-capsule discharge demos exist for all three regimes (`ansys/fluent_tank_discharge.py`, `ansys/fluent_discharge_demo.py`).
